# Resources for Teaching {#sec:teachingresources}

Teaching is considered to be an important component of faculty
activities. That said, most new faculty come in with strong research
experience, but modest teaching experience, if any. It helps that most
new faculty are given about a semester off from teaching in the
beginning - this is often academic unit's policy; in some cases, there may not be a choice if the faculty member joins after a semester has started. Here are a few tips to help with teaching, and preparing for it.

1. When you are assigned a course to teach, you can look at the
   Academic section of the ASC website
   (https://asc.iitb.ac.in/acadmenu/index.jsp) for course details
   such as syllabus and textbooks, as well as timing and venue. In
   general, it is mandatory to adhere to the specified syllabus,
   especially for core courses. However, instructors can enhance
   their course offerings with additional topics and learning content.
2. You may talk to the Head and ask for details of the previous instructors
   (this information is also available on ASC). That is assuming this
   is an existing course, not a new one you are starting; the
   procedure for starting a new course is described in the [form for proposing a new academic course](http://www.iitb.ac.in/newacadhome/RevisedCourseProposalFormat20154March.pdf). Senior faculty members who have taught the course may be
   able to help you with teaching material such as slides, homework
   problems, recommendations for textbooks, capable teaching
   assistants (TAs) and so forth.
3. An alumni supported initiative, called the Parimal and
   Pramod Chaudhari Centre for Learning and Teaching (PPCCLT), now
   provides a plethora of resources for teaching, drawing on internal
   and external expertise and experience. These include:
    a. (Annual) Faculty Development Workshops
	b. TLC Café - featuring training sessions for faculty on effective teaching
	c. Community of Practice (CoP) platform for sharing best teaching practices
    d. Active learning classroom (under construction at the time of	writing). Please check out the [PPCCLT	website](http://www.ppcclt.iitb.ac.in) for more details.They welcome and need faculty involvement to be effective, so please	  consider it.

4. There are several resources available to you to prepare video lectures (getting your regular lectures recorded, or, recording in a studio), and put them online if you desire. These include:

   a. Centre for Distance Engineering Education Programme (CDEEP) –
      which helps to prepare video lectures. Details are available on
      their [website](http://www.cdeep.iitb.ac.in/). Please look in
      the Related Projects section, for information on
      pedagogy-related projects, usually MoE-supported, like TEQIP,
      GIAN and NMEICT.

   b. [National Programme on Technology Enhanced Learning (NPTEL)](https://nptel.ac.in/) - a nationwide
      program supported by MoE for high-quality content development
      in science/technology and dissemination through Massive Open
      Online Courses (MOOCs), with facility for testing and
      certification.

5. IIT Bombay is one of the few institutes in the country to have an
   academic program in Education Technology. Faculty here pursue
   research in technology-enhanced learning, pedagogical tools and
   strategies. If you are interested in exploring new
   technologies/methodologies in your class, they might be happy to
   collaborate with you. Details about this Inter-Disciplinary
   Programme is available [here](http://www.et.iitb.ac.in/). Some of
   these are outlined below:

   a. [Online Teaching](https://sites.google.com/view/iitb-teachonline/) (popularly known as OTeach). This was developed
   by ET faculty and PhD research scholars during the Covid-19
   lockdown. It is constructed as a self-paced course for instructors
   to move towards teaching online.

   b. [Activity constructors and
   templates](https://www.et.iitb.ac.in/products/teaching-resources)
   for using active learning strategies, and [videos](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCfn80M6YJ4Bd5laqxkJVN3Q ) on pedagogy and teaching
   strategies in specific topics.

   c. The collaborative learning classroom at PPCCLT
   is active and functioning. Several institute courses as well as workshops
   are held every semester. Faculty who are interested can get more
   [details here](http://www.ppcclt.iitb.ac.in/collaborative-learning-and-research-laboratory/).

The preferred mode for posting materials, assignments, grades and
other information regarding a course is the internally hosted
[Moodle](https://moodle.iitb.ac.in) learning platform. More guidance on
using Moodle effectively is available [here](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1U6Z1m-9cR-fP9KWMIqjAWZdOXtJ_lNCf).

Some instructors use external platforms alongside or instead of
Moodle:

- [Piazza](https://piazza.com) is a class discussion forum where
  students post questions and answer each other. **Students can post
  anonymously to their classmates**, so shy students ask questions
  they would not ask in class. You can also post course material and
  announcements and run polls there.
- [Gradescope](https://www.gradescope.com) is built for **online
  grading and regrades**. You and your TAs grade scanned handwritten
  answer scripts against a shared rubric, which speeds up grading
  large classes and keeps it consistent. Students see their graded
  scripts online and file regrade requests against specific
  questions, which replaces the in-person "crib" session. It also
  runs online quizzes, exams and assignments.

We also encourage you to see the [PwD awareness website](https://sites.google.com/view/iitb-pwdcell-training) to get some
insight on how you can make the learning experience more suited for
students who face certain disabilities.

## Conducting examinations

::: {.review}
The suggestions below are for faculty who set or invigilate a
mid-semester or end-semester exam.

**Two weeks before the exam**

1. Fill in the Academic Office form that is circulated before each
   exam. It asks whether the exam is closed book, open book or
   SAFE-based, which decides the venue, and how many answer books
   you need: 12-page books for the mid-semester exam and 16-page
   books for the end-semester exam.
2. Brief your TA invigilators. They must arrive 30 minutes early
   with their original ID card. They may not bring bags, phones,
   earphones, papers, reading material or laptops. They report any
   suspected malpractice to you quietly.
3. Remind students of the rules. They should reach the venue half
   an hour early and be in their seats ten minutes before the start.
   Entry closes 30 minutes after the exam starts, and no student is
   admitted without an original ID card. Students may bring only
   their ID card, the stationery the exam needs and a water bottle,
   plus the authorised material for an open-book exam. Phones,
   smartwatches, laptops, earphones and other devices are not
   allowed anywhere in the exam building, so students should leave
   them in their hostel rooms.

**On the day of the exam**

4. Arrive half an hour before the start. Stay until every answer book
   has been collected, counted and packed.
5. Collect the answer books from the staff yourself. Academic Office
   staff supply them for common courses, and department staff
   supply them for all other courses. Staff hand answer books only
   to the faculty invigilator, never to TAs or project staff. You get
   one main answer book for each registered student, a small packet
   of spares, and two 4-page supplementary sheets for each student.
6. Write the rules on the board, adjusted for the type of exam: no
   phones, smartwatches or other electronic devices; no books,
   notes, formula sheets or chits; taking an answer sheet out of the
   hall counts as an unauthorised practice; and unauthorised
   practices may lead to disciplinary action.
7. Do not bring reading material or a laptop into the hall. You may
   carry a phone, but do not join virtual meetings or calls during
   the exam.

**During the exam**

8. Make sure the TA or staff invigilators take attendance and check
   each student's ID card. If a student has no ID card, check their
   photo on ASC. If that does not settle it, photograph the student
   at the desk and note this on the attendance sheet.
9. Sign and date each supplementary sheet before you hand it to a
   student.
10. Let only one student out of the hall at a time for a bio-break.
11. Exam halls are monitored centrally through CCTV. If the
    monitoring picks up any unauthorised activity, you will be told,
    and you should follow the procedure under
    [Academic malpractice](#academic-malpractice).

**After the exam**

12. On the
    [attendance sheet](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1bSVBXcwVZCfUtGNUD3c8Gkm20wvqqDMt/view),
    record how many main and supplementary sheets were issued, used
    and left unused.
13. Hand the unused sheets back to the staff yourself, not through a
    TA.

Steps 5, 9, 12 and 13 do not apply when students write their answers
on the question paper itself.
:::

*Sources:* [Report of the committee to revisit Examination Conduct
Rules and Process](https://surveys.iitb.ac.in/pluginfile.php/19040/course/section/2824/Report%20of%20the%20committee%20to%20revisit%20Examination%20Conduct%20Rules%20and%20Process-After%20Meeting.pdf).

## Academic malpractice

If you catch a student copying in an exam or plagiarising an
assignment, follow the Institute's
standard operating procedure rather than deciding the penalty on your
own. The Academic Office lists the procedure on its
[Academic Malpractices page](https://acad.iitb.ac.in/academicMalpractices).
The penalties for each kind of offence are in the
[Senate-approved list of punishments](https://acad.iitb.ac.in/sites/default/files/Acad%20Malpractice%20punishments%20Senate%20approved.pdf).

::: {.review}
**If you see unfair means during an exam.** Your job in the hall is
only to stop the act, collect the material and record what happened.
The Disciplinary Action Committee (DAC) handles the rest later. The
report includes two forms: Form 01, which the invigilator fills in,
and Form 02, an optional statement form for the student.

*During the exam*

1. Quietly collect the unauthorised material: chits, phone or other
   device, answer papers. Say as little as possible to the student
   and avoid disturbing the others.
2. If the item has to be given back, such as a phone, photograph it.
   If you are not sure who the student is, photograph them at the
   desk.
3. Take the student's original answer book and give them a fresh one.
   They carry on writing until the end of the exam.

*After the exam*

4. Fill in and sign Form 01.
5. Give the student a chance to record their version of events on
   Form 02, at a designated venue with additional staff present.
   The student does not have to fill in Form 02, unless a phone was
   taken.
6. Return any phone you took. The student signs for it on Form 02.
7. Submit Form 01 to the Head of the Department conducting the
   course. Attach the collected material, the original answer book
   and Form 02, if the student filled it in. Digital material can be
   sent by email.
8. When the student leaves the exam hall, alert the Wellness Response
   Team by phone at +91 8356 810252 and by email at
   [wellness@iitb.ac.in](mailto:wellness@iitb.ac.in). Give the course
   code, the student's name and roll number, and the exam venue.

*Penalties*

The penalties approved by the 270th Senate are on hold until a
revised disciplinary framework is agreed. Until then, disciplinary
action follows the [document the Senate approved in April 2015](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1gsIDDTCw3mEPtlxpPgekT4J9LZqfoFvs/view). Once
the D-ADAC's recommendations are approved, instructors apply any
penalty on marks. Instructors must not apply grade penalties when
awarding grades, because the Academic Office applies those. Cases
are summarised on the
[D-ADAC summary sheet](https://drive.google.com/file/d/16Z8pLZVW4i7rRPOxbAMlv1Emhy35U7fV/view).
:::

*Sources:* [Report of the committee to revisit Examination Conduct
Rules and Process](https://surveys.iitb.ac.in/pluginfile.php/19040/course/section/2824/Report%20of%20the%20committee%20to%20revisit%20Examination%20Conduct%20Rules%20and%20Process-After%20Meeting.pdf)
(includes Forms 01 and 02);
[minutes of the Heads' meeting, 30 September 2026](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1hRB7_UNrzu16TjCjF4_DFLtQgtTbFSklBJxg4dVQgEw/edit).

## Student wellness

You may be the first to notice a student who is struggling, from
missed classes or a sudden drop in grades. Talk to the student, and
point them to the people below.

- [The Wellness Response Team (WRT) supports students in crisis at any hour. It has counsellors and plain-clothes security staff, with a psychiatrist on call. Reach it by phone or WhatsApp at +91 8356 810252 (call in an emergency) or by email at [wellness@iitb.ac.in](mailto:wellness@iitb.ac.in).]{.review}
- [Student Wellness Centre (SWC)](http://swc.iitb.ac.in/home) offers
  free, confidential counselling to students.
- [Flourishing IITB](https://www.flourishing-iitb.org/) is an
  initiative on student well-being at IIT Bombay.
- [Saathi](https://www.saathiiitb.com/) is the LGBTQ+ resource group
  of IIT Bombay.
- The [Gender Cell](http://www.iitb.ac.in/resources/gendercell)
  handles complaints of sexual harassment and works on gender
  sensitisation (see the chapter on Ethics and Code of Conduct).
- The [SC/ST Students Cell](https://www.scstcell.iitb.ac.in/) handles
  the concerns and grievances of SC/ST students, including
  caste-based discrimination.
